headline: New chromosome-scale assemblies for kelp, a coral, and a microsporidian symbiont
label: Eukaryotic Genome Assembly Resources
summary: Long-read and telomere-to-telomere assemblies now resolve chromosome-scale genomes across brown alga, reef coral, and microsporidian symbiont lineages.
synthesis: The three items share a common product: chromosome-scale eukaryotic genome assemblies with associated gene sets. The giant kelp preprint reports two diploid Macrocystis pyrifera assemblies from long reads, each with 35 pseudo-chromosomes, and associates them with distinct Southern Hemisphere genetics. The Microsporidia sp. MB preprint presents a telomere-to-telomere de novo assembly of 9.16 Mb across 13 chromosomes, with 2,435 genes, from Anopheles coluzzii samples collected in Burkina Faso. The Porites harrisoni preprint reports a 626.7 Mb coral genome with 27,823 protein-coding genes and a mitogenome from the southern Persian/Arabian Gulf. What is new is the extension of chromosome-scale assembly to a brown alga, a microsporidian symbiont, and a reef-building coral from distinct geographic sources. None of these items reports an annotation-error assessment, so the earlier emphasis on gene model accuracy is not directly addressed here.
